title: Use cohort survival instead of one churn rate when billing data exist
decision_task: Whether to use a single churn rate or the observed survival curve.
applies_when: Payments are connected (convex/analytics.ts:311 computeCohorts) and at least 3 cohorts have 3 or more complete months.
exclusions: Cohorts smaller than about 20 customers; show counts instead.
Annual contracts before their first renewal (DS-02-F8).
missing_data_behavior: Fewer than 3 cohorts with 3+ complete months, or cohorts under ~20 customers: show counts, keep single churn labelled assumed.
alternatives_when_constrained: No cohorts: use the owner's churn as an assumption.
Small sample: show raw counts and a wide range.

decision_branches.then: Observed survival replaces monthly churn, tagged measured.

implementation_steps: Average retention by cohort age, weighted by cohort size.
Feed the survival curve S_t into the payback and value sum instead of (1 − c)^t.
Compare newer cohorts with older ones to show whether fixes worked.
guardrails: Immature months stay null, never zero (cohorts.ts:5-7 already does this).
Do not extrapolate past the observed months without a label.
observation_window: Up to 6 months as computed today (analytics.ts:311 maxMonths 6), extended to 12 for value.
stop_conditions: Review when a new cohort completes month 3.
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes

interpretation: Interpretation: ClimbOS computes cohorts but economics ignores them, so value assumes a constant hazard even when early churn dominates.
proposed_climbos_rule: Proposed rule: when cohort data meet the minimum, observed survival replaces monthlyChurn in playMaths, tagged 'measured'.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical
hard_failure: Converts to one blended churn with no label

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
